name: Mosaic Retrieve Rank Re-rank Reason Lab Contract

ownership.source_repository: Lab timing, retrieval examples, application surfaces, evaluation assertions, and the gap seams with their broken bodies (scripts/lab_state.py).
ownership.workshop_studio: Participant instructions, provisioning-time gap injection, and code-editor exercises.

memory.question: Can Mosaic remember Alex’s preferences across conversations?
memory.story: Alex comes back another day. Recall what matters to him, then check the catalog again before recommending a product.
memory.placement: After the required hour; extraction time is asynchronous and has no promised duration.
memory.opening_message: I prefer a 27-inch monitor with USB-C laptop charging, so I can run code and read docs side by side with fewer cables.
memory.request: Which monitor would suit the way I work at home?
memory.changed_request: For this request, I want a 32-inch monitor, not my usual 27-inch preference. USB-C laptop charging is optional today. Compare suitable monitors and cite their screen size and connection specifications.
checkpoints: Save Alex’s message and inspect its event ID. Wait for an actual extracted preference record before continuing.
Start a new session. Keep the same actor, with no earlier conversation events or copied shortlist.
Find relevant memories and ask the same question with memory on and off. Inspect record IDs actually read; different wording alone is not proof.
Follow the new Aurora search and resolve each product citation. Memory supplies preferences, never product facts.
Submit the changed request. Verify the new size takes priority even when the older preference is recalled.
Start fresh as another actor. Alex’s records must be unavailable, including when the earlier session ID is supplied.

missions.title: Lab 1 - Debug hybrid search

participant_edit.task: Find the search whose candidates never reach fusion, then add its channels branch in search_hybrid_rrf.
participant_edit.broken_state: Alex transposes CF to FC in listing ID B0C2WWCFQB. Exact terms and the bounded meaning-search list miss that listing. Close-spelling search finds it, but search_hybrid_rrf never reads its CTE, so it never reaches fusion.
participant_edit.fixed_state: The restored close-spelling channel admits Logitech Zone 900, product 1492978, with trigram rank 1. It was final rank 1 in repeated verification.
observe_before: HTTP 200 with other headphones; the intended Logitech listing 1492978 is absent from the first 10 results.
The saved combined pool omits 1492978 and reports trigram_in_pool = 0.
observe_after: The identical B0C2WWFCQB request returns listing B0C2WWCFQB (1492978).
The target has a trigram rank and contribution; its FTS and semantic ranks remain null.
All products satisfy the headphones category and electronics domain filters.
participant_edit.checkpoint_question: Why can related headphones be wrong for an exact-product request, and why could reranking not recover the missing listing?

missions.expected_outcome: Recover the exact Logitech listing B0C2WWCFQB from a transposed identifier, with a close-spelling rank and contribution. Other headphones are wrong identities for this request; no claim is made that they lack noise cancellation.

missions.title: Lab 2 - Tune rank fusion and reranking
missions.discover_label: Keep the right monitor in the shortlist

participant_edit.task: Restore the reciprocal-rank contribution formula 1 / (k + rank).
participant_edit.broken_state: Collapsed contributions erase positions within each search, so every single-search candidate ties and the 50-product cutoff is decided by product id: the oldest listings stay, and every recent 27-inch 4K USB-C listing, including the ViewSonic VG2756-4K, never reaches reranking.
participant_edit.fixed_state: Correct contributions retain the ViewSonic VG2756-4K (1551237), found by meaning rank 10. In verification on the Mosaic catalog it moved from absent to combined position 21 and final position 5; its source record states 27-inch 4K IPS, USB-C with 90W charging over one cable, RJ45, HDMI and DisplayPort.
observe_before: HTTP 200 with plausible 4K monitors, but ViewSonic VG2756-4K 1551237 is absent from the combined list of 50, so reranking never received it.
The saved combined pool holds the lowest product ids among the single-search candidates; a 1440p Lenovo T27hv-20 appears among the final results for a 4K request.
observe_after: The identical request returns ViewSonic VG2756-4K 1551237 at final position 5 from combined position 21, with a meaning rank of 10 and no word or spelling rank.
The other recent 4K USB-C listings (INNOCN 27, ASUS ProArt PA27UCX-K, HP Z27) enter the combined list for the first time; the shortlist changes from old listings to fits.
participant_edit.checkpoint_question: Why could the reranker not select the ViewSonic before the repair, and why need its combined position not be first?

missions.expected_outcome: Restore 1 / (k + source_rank), keep the ViewSonic VG2756-4K in the bounded combined list, and let reranking compare its 4K and 90W USB-C specifications with Alex's request.

missions.title: Lab 3 - Build and deploy the agent
missions.discover_label: Complete Alex’s room with your agent
missions.query: I am finishing my home office. Check the Logitech Zone 900 (B0C2WWCFQB) for noise cancellation that helps me focus and what the available reviews establish about clear calls; the ViewSonic VG2756-4K (B0BSHZHKB7) for a 27-inch 4K screen and USB-C charging up to 90W over one cable; and the Steelcase Gesture (B095V7RS6S) for adjustable lumbar support and fully adjustable arms, and whether reviewers say it stays comfortable through a full workday. Search each product separately, compare all three as parts of my room, and explain what the specifications and available reviews do and do not establish. Cite supporting records for each product and explain the ranking of one search.

participant_edit.task: Build a Strands agent with the supplied model, SQL tool adapters, instructions and execution hooks, then deploy it to AgentCore Runtime.
participant_edit.broken_state: The agent starter is incomplete. Mosaic names the file to edit and the deployment command.
participant_edit.fixed_state: The deployed Strands agent calls Aurora tools through AgentCore Gateway and answers with product sources.
observe_before: Mosaic explains that the agent is not built yet.
The message points to labs/lab3_reason/agent.py and the deploy command.
observe_after: Your agent runs in AgentCore Runtime and calls the SQL tools through Gateway.
Separate searches find the headphones, monitor and chair using your Labs 1 and 2 SQL.
Recommendations cite retrieved product records and explain what those records leave uncertain.
A follow-up request changes the recommendation while preserving source checks.
participant_edit.checkpoint_question: Which tools did your agent choose, and how did its answer change when Alex changed a requirement?

missions.expected_outcome: A bounded, read-only agent runs a focused search for each of the three requested products, compares headphones, monitor and chair as parts of Alex’s room, explains a search ranking, and cites real source records within application-owned citation scope while keeping microphone quality, laptop compatibility and all-day comfort uncertain when the evidence does not establish them.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Preserve the exact listing
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: The correctly spelled ASIN retrieves the intended Logitech listing with an Exact terms contribution.

supporting_checks.title: Control - A misspelled famous name
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: Inside Headphones, meaning search still finds the Zone 900 while close spelling is disconnected (meaning rank 2 on the 2026-10-03 dev run), and reranking puts it first. There is no before-and-after contrast: not every typo needs close spelling.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Recover a misspelled edition
supporting_checks.query: Quick Acess to ANC and Bluetoth
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: Alex recalls a feature from the listing he saved, quick access to ANC and Bluetooth, and misspells two words. Exact terms and meaning search miss it; the restored close-spelling channel finds it at trigram rank 1 and reranking puts it first.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Describe the monitor need
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: Inspect which methods retrieve the Dell when the request describes screen resolution and laptop charging rather than a model name.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Keep the brand requirement
supporting_checks.query: Logitech Zone 900 on-ear wireless headset with noise-canceling microphone
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: The model-name search retains the Logitech target. Every saved candidate and displayed result stays within the Logitech headphones filter; a related product from another brand is ineligible.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Compare display specifications
supporting_checks.query: Dell U2720Q versus Dell SE2717H monitor resolution USB-C charging
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: Retrieve both named Dell monitors. Their records distinguish 3840 x 2160 from 1920 x 1080. Do not infer equivalent USB-C charging, current price or stock.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Keep brand filters ahead of scoring
supporting_checks.discover_label: Keep brand filters ahead of scoring
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: The same monitor need, restricted to Dell, excludes HP and Lenovo before reranking. Inspect both saved candidates and served results.

supporting_checks.title: Checkpoint - Separate listening from microphone evidence
supporting_checks.query: For Logitech Zone 900 B0C2WWCFQB, what do the specifications and available reviews support about noise cancellation and clear calls? Cite the records, and say where review evidence does not establish microphone performance.
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: Resolve specification and sampled-review citations for the Logitech listing. A listed noise-canceling microphone and one reviewer’s experience do not establish call quality for Alex, and other reviews of this listing disagree; present the review as one experience and disclose the gap.

supporting_checks.title: Tune the HNSW operating point
supporting_checks.expected_outcome: A measured configuration records recall, latency, index size, build time, extension version, and filter selectivity.

guided_requests.label: Complete my room
guided_requests.notice: Bring Lab 1’s Logitech headphones and Lab 2’s ViewSonic monitor together with the Steelcase chair. Follow three focused searches, a comparison of all three, and the sources behind the complete room.

guided_requests.label: Check the focus picks
guided_requests.query: For Logitech Zone 900 (B0C2WWCFQB) and 3M Quiet Space (B09LK7TRYV), will my teammates hear me clearly on calls? Search each product separately, compare its specifications and available reviews, and cite the supporting records. Distinguish listening noise cancellation, playback sound and outgoing microphone quality. Say what the records leave unknown and explain the ranking of one search.
guided_requests.notice: The deck’s evidence question about Logitech and 3M. The agent creates fresh search and source records; the deck’s authored comparison is an illustration, not a saved agent answer.

guided_requests.label: Check the sources
guided_requests.notice: Return to Alex’s Logitech headphones. Separate listening noise cancellation from microphone quality; its reviews disagree about how teammates hear him.

requests.label: Focus at home
requests.query: headphones that help me focus when working from home
requests.notice: The deck’s worked search: follow the same headphones through Retrieve, Rank and Re-rank. Then ask the agent what their sources support. Live positions can differ from the deck’s saved run.

requests.label: Recover my headphones
requests.notice: Lab 1: recover the Logitech listing Alex saved from its transposed identifier. Keep the same request and filters before and after your repair.

requests.label: Comfortable days
requests.query: a chair that keeps me comfortable through long coding sessions, with support I can adjust to fit me
requests.notice: Follow Alex’s need for adjustable support from finding products through ranking and a comparison grounded in product details.

requests.label: More screen space
requests.notice: Alex wants room for code and reference material, with fewer cables on his desk. Compare screen size, resolution and connections. Check the specifications for USB-C video and charging separately.
